You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.",
  "The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.",
  "A paid-up licence is perpetual.",
  "A paid-up licence is irrevocable.",
  "A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.",
  "The licence is transferable to Customer's successors."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.",
  "The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction."
]

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.",
  "Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.",
  "Audits occur during business hours.",
  "Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.",
  "The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.",
  "Audits are conducted off-site where possible.",
  "Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.",
  "Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Vendor may audit no more than once per year.",
  "Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.",
  "Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent."
]

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.",
  "Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.",
  "Audits occur during business hours.",
  "Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.",
  "The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.",
  "Audits are conducted off-site where possible.",
  "Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.",
  "Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Vendor may audit no more than once per year.",
  "Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.",
  "Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent."
]

Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-11","number":"11","heading":"TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND DATA RETURN","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-11.1","number":"11.1","heading":"Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-11.2","number":"11.2","heading":"Within thirty days after Customer's request, Vendor shall return all Customer Data in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format, with relationships and metadata reasonably necessary for use. Vendor shall not withhold Customer Data because of a fee dispute.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-11.3","number":"11.3","heading":"After Customer confirms successful return, Vendor shall securely delete remaining Customer Data from active systems and, as backups cycle, from backups, except for a copy required by Applicable Law. An authorized officer shall certify deletion in writing. Any retained copy remains protected and may not be used for another purpose.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12","number":"12","heading":"CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12.3","number":"12.3","heading":"Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12.4","number":"12.4","heading":"For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13","number":"13","heading":"ACCESS RIGHTS AND LICENCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.1","number":"13.1","heading":"Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.2","number":"13.2","heading":"For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.3","number":"13.3","heading":"Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.4","number":"13.4","heading":"Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14","number":"14","heading":"INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DELIVERABLES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.1","number":"14.1","heading":"As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.2","number":"14.2","heading":"Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.3","number":"14.3","heading":"Vendor retains Vendor Technology. To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.4","number":"14.4","heading":"No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Feedback is voluntary; Vendor may use generalized suggestions without identifying Customer or disclosing Customer Confidential Information, and Customer retains the unrestricted right to use its own feedback.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15","number":"15","heading":"CUSTOMER DATA AND PRIVACY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15.1","number":"15.1","heading":"Vendor shall process Customer Data only on Customer's documented instructions, to provide the Services, and as permitted by this Agreement. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data, use it for advertising, combine it with another customer's identifiable data, or train a generally available model on it without Customer's express written consent.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15.2","number":"15.2","heading":"Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law concerning personal information. If Vendor processes personal information for Customer, the Parties' data-processing addendum is incorporated. Vendor is a processor or service provider and shall assist Customer with data-subject requests, impact assessments, consultations, and regulatory inquiries.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16","number":"16","heading":"CONFIDENTIALITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.1","number":"16.1","heading":"“Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.2","number":"16.2","heading":"The recipient shall use Confidential Information only to perform or exercise rights under this Agreement, protect it with at least reasonable care, and disclose it only to personnel, Affiliates, advisers, and subcontractors who need to know and are bound by confidentiality obligations. The recipient is responsible for their unauthorized use or disclosure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.5","number":"16.5","heading":"On request or termination, the recipient shall return or destroy Confidential Information, subject to routine backups and legal retention. Duties for trade secrets continue while protected as trade secrets; duties for other Confidential Information continue for five years after disclosure. Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17","number":"17","heading":"INFORMATION SECURITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17.1","number":"17.1","heading":"Vendor shall maintain a written information-security program using administrative, technical, organizational, and physical safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity of Customer Data and risk. At minimum, Vendor shall implement least-privilege access, multifactor authentication, encryption in transit and at rest, secure development, vulnerability management, logging, backup, business continuity, and annual workforce training.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17.2","number":"17.2","heading":"Vendor shall notify Customer without undue delay and no later than twenty-four hours after confirming unauthorized access to, acquisition, disclosure, alteration, loss, or destruction of Customer Data or a material compromise of systems used to provide the Services (a “Security Incident”). Notice will include known facts, affected data and systems, containment, and a contact.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18","number":"18","heading":"INSURANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18.1","number":"18.1","heading":"Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18.2","number":"18.2","heading":"Policies will be issued by reputable insurers and be primary to Customer's insurance where commercially customary. On request, Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance and evidence of relevant coverage. Vendor shall give advance notice of cancellation or material reduction to the extent available from its insurer. Insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19","number":"19","heading":"WARRANTIES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.1","number":"19.1","heading":"Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.2","number":"19.2","heading":"For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.3","number":"19.3","heading":"Vendor warrants the Services and Deliverables will not contain malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, and that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law. Vendor will not materially diminish functionality during a term or use open-source software in a way that requires disclosure or licensing of Customer source code.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.4","number":"19.4","heading":"For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.5","number":"19.5","heading":"Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20","number":"20","heading":"INDEMNIFICATION","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.1","number":"20.1","heading":"Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.2","number":"20.2","heading":"Vendor shall also defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the Customer indemnified parties from third-party claims to the extent arising from Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; bodily injury, death, or tangible property damage caused by Vendor; unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.3","number":"20.3","heading":"Customer shall defend and indemnify Vendor from a third-party claim alleging that unmodified Customer material supplied by Customer and used by Vendor strictly as authorized infringes an intellectual property right, or arising from Customer's violation of Applicable Law in its authorized use of the Services. Customer has no obligation to the extent a claim arises from Vendor Technology, modification, combination, or instructions.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.4","number":"20.4","heading":"The indemnified Party shall give prompt notice, reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, and control of the defence, except delay excuses obligations only to the extent of material prejudice. The indemnifying Party may not settle a claim by admitting fault of, imposing non-monetary obligations on, or failing to fully release the indemnified Party without prior written consent.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.5","number":"20.5","heading":"For an infringement claim, Vendor shall, at its expense and in addition to its defence obligations, procure continued use, modify or replace the affected item without materially reducing functionality, or, if neither is commercially reasonable, terminate the item and refund prepaid and implementation Fees on a straight-line three-year basis. Vendor may not terminate unaffected Services.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21","number":"21","heading":"LIMITATION OF LIABILITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.1","number":"21.1","heading":"Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.2","number":"21.2","heading":"Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill, to the extent those damages are legally excludable. Costs of restoring Customer Data, obtaining replacement services, required notices, and reasonable incident response are direct damages.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.3","number":"21.3","heading":"“Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.4","number":"21.4","heading":"The limitations allocate risk between sophisticated Parties and apply only to the maximum extent permitted by Applicable Law. Nothing limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited. Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22","number":"22","heading":"AUDIT RIGHTS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22.1","number":"22.1","heading":"Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22.2","number":"22.2","heading":"Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22.3","number":"22.3","heading":"Audit findings are Customer Confidential Information and may be used only to enforce this Agreement. Vendor shall provide a copy of the final report. Payment of a shortfall resolves the audited quantity issue absent fraud or demonstrable error.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-23","number":"23","heading":"RECORDS AND CUSTOMER ASSURANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24","number":"24","heading":"ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.1","number":"24.1","heading":"Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.2","number":"24.2","heading":"Vendor may not assign this Agreement, delegate material performance, or transfer it by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld for an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing. Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.3","number":"24.3","heading":"For other assignments, neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. A permitted assignment does not relieve accrued obligations. An attempted assignment contrary to this Section is void to the extent permitted by law.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.4","number":"24.4","heading":"Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service. Vendor shall cooperate with reasonable administrative changes needed to reflect a permitted successor.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-25","number":"25","heading":"PUBLICITY AND MARKS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-25.1","number":"25.1","heading":"Neither Party may issue a press release naming the other or use the other's names, trademarks, logos, or service marks in publicity, customer lists, case studies, or marketing without prior written consent in each instance. Customer may withdraw consent prospectively.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26","number":"26","heading":"COMPLIANCE WITH LAW AND ETHICS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.1","number":"26.1","heading":"Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law in performing this Agreement. Vendor shall maintain policies reasonably designed to prevent bribery, corruption, forced labour, discrimination, retaliation, and conflicts of interest and shall provide annual compliance training to assigned personnel.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.2","number":"26.2","heading":"Vendor represents it has not offered and will not offer anything of value to improperly influence an official or private person in connection with this Agreement. Vendor shall maintain accurate books and promptly report a credible suspected violation materially related to the Services.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.3","number":"26.3","heading":"Each Party shall comply with applicable export-control and sanctions laws. Vendor is responsible for classifying Vendor Technology and identifying restrictions before delivery. Customer will not knowingly permit access from a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction contrary to written notice and Applicable Law.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.4","number":"26.4","heading":"Vendor shall comply with reasonable Customer workplace, safety, security, and acceptable-use policies supplied in advance while accessing Customer facilities or systems. A policy does not amend commercial terms or impose obligations unrelated to that access.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-27","number":"27","heading":"FORCE MAJEURE AND BUSINESS CONTINUITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-27.1","number":"27.1","heading":"Neither Party is liable for delay caused by an event beyond its reasonable control that could not have been prevented through reasonable care, excluding inability to pay, staffing shortages, subcontractor failure that could reasonably be avoided, or a cyberattack preventable by required safeguards. The affected Party shall promptly notify the other and mitigate.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-27.2","number":"27.2","heading":"Vendor shall maintain and test at least annually business-continuity and disaster-recovery plans appropriate to the Services. Plans will address redundant systems, backups, recovery objectives, communications, and alternate personnel. Vendor shall provide a current executive summary on request.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-27.3","number":"27.3","heading":"If a force-majeure event materially prevents an affected Service for more than fifteen consecutive days, Customer may procure substitute services and suspend affected Fees. After thirty consecutive days, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without penalty and receive a refund of prepaid Fees for the unavailable period.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-28","number":"28","heading":"GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-28.1","number":"28.1","heading":"This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-28.2","number":"28.2","heading":"The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-28.3","number":"28.3","heading":"Before filing an ordinary commercial claim, a Party shall give notice and permit executives with settlement authority to meet in good faith within fifteen business days. This process does not delay urgent relief or a filing needed to preserve a limitations period. Discussions are compromise negotiations to the extent allowed by law.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-29","number":"29","heading":"NOTICES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-29.1","number":"29.1","heading":"Legal notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by nationally recognized overnight courier or certified mail, return receipt requested, to the address in the preamble and by email to the legal-notice address stated in the applicable Order Form. Operational notices may be delivered through agreed service channels.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-29.2","number":"29.2","heading":"Notice is effective on documented delivery, except a refusal is deemed delivery. A Party may change its notice address by notice under this Section. Email alone is insufficient for breach, termination, indemnity, assignment, or litigation notices unless receipt is affirmatively acknowledged.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-29.3","number":"29.3","heading":"Notices to Customer must copy legal@northwind.example, and notices to Vendor must copy legal@brightline.example. Automated portal messages, invoices, and website postings are not legal notices.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-30","number":"30","heading":"GENERAL","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-30.1","number":"30.1","heading":"The Parties are independent contractors. Nothing creates a partnership, joint venture, fiduciary relationship, franchise, or agency. Neither Party may bind the other. Vendor is solely responsible for compensation, direction, and taxes of its personnel.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-30.2","number":"30.2","heading":"Neither Party's failure or delay in exercising a right waives it. A waiver must be written and signed by an authorized representative and applies only to the stated instance. Remedies are cumulative unless an exclusive remedy is expressly identified.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-30.3","number":"30.3","heading":"If a court finds a provision unenforceable, it will be modified to the minimum extent needed to make it enforceable while preserving intent, and the remainder continues. Headings aid reference only. “Including” means “including without limitation,” and “or” is inclusive.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-30.4","number":"30.4","heading":"This Agreement, its exhibits, and executed Order Forms are the entire agreement about their subject and supersede prior proposals, statements, and agreements. An amendment must be in a writing signed by authorized representatives of both Parties and expressly identify this Agreement.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-30.5","number":"30.5","heading":"No person other than a Party, a Customer Affiliate ordering Services, a permitted successor, or an indemnified party has a right to enforce this Agreement. The Parties may amend or terminate it without another person's consent, subject to vested indemnity rights.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-30.6","number":"30.6","heading":"This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, each treated as an original, and by electronic signature. An electronic copy is effective as an original. Each signatory represents that they are authorized to bind the named Party.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-30.7","number":"30.7","heading":"Vendor shall not use an artificial-intelligence system to make a legally binding decision for Customer or submit Customer Confidential Information to a third-party model unless an Order Form expressly authorizes that use and specifies safeguards. Vendor remains responsible for output used in providing the Services.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-30.8","number":"30.8","heading":"The Parties have caused their authorized representatives to execute this Agreement as of the Effective Date.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-p0130","heading":"REDWOOD COMMERCE GROUP, INC. (CUSTOMER)","level":1,"paragraphCount":2},{"id":"sec-p0132","heading":"SILVERLINE SYSTEMS LTD. (VENDOR)","level":1,"paragraphCount":2}]

tools.name: list_sections
tools.description: List the document section outline when planner hints are insufficient.

tools.name: read_section
tools.description: Read every paragraph in one likely clause section by stable section id.

tools.name: read_paragraphs
tools.description: Read specific planner, search, nearby, or cross-referenced paragraphs by stable id.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the entire document. Use multiple targeted searches and inspect every responsive clause, not only the first hit.

tools.name: get_definition
tools.description: Resolve every defined term material to scope, amount, direction, duration, or a cross-reference.

tools.name: lookup_precedent
tools.description: Retrieve approved language as an element-labelled template; adapt it to the current clause and re-check every marker.

tools.name: propose_redline
tools.description: Validate anchors, rendering, and the deterministic minimality gate. Correct every error before submission.

tools.name: submit_finding
tools.description: Submit once. Actionable findings require exact coverage of every selected checklist element.

input.rationale: Section 24 meets our preferred position in full. 24.1 gives Customer a consent-free right to assign to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all assets (prompt notice only, which is not a consent condition). 24.2 bars Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent, with the reasonableness standard running in our favour, and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor. 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any termination, suspension, repricing, acceleration or service-reduction right on our change of control, so we are clear of walk-away territory. 24.3's residual mutual consent requirement applies only to "other assignments" and therefore does not cut back the 24.1 carve-out, and 13.3 aligns by letting Customer transfer licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with a Section 24-permitted assignment. Only minor point short of ideal wording: 24.2's competitor bar is expressed as "without Customer's consent" rather than absolute, but that leaves the discretion with us and is noted rather than redlined.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: ASSIGN
Title: Assignment and change of control
Kind: parametric
Summary: We may assign to affiliates and successors; the Vendor may not exit on our change of control.
Severity: high
Category: assignment
Position — preferred:
Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets; Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not to be unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control.

Position — fallback:
Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice; consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
Position — walk-away:
Blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out, or a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control.

Detection guidance:
"may not assign", "change of control", "deemed an assignment", consent standards. Determine whether the restriction binds Customer symmetrically and whether change-of-control triggers any Vendor right.

Redline guidance:
Add the affiliate/successor carve-out for Customer; delete change-of-control termination rights against Customer.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.",
  "Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.",
  "Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.",
  "Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.",
  "Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.",
  "Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Both parties may assign to a successor.",
  "A successor assignment requires written notice.",
  "Other assignments require consent.",
  "Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld."
]
