**Finding: compliant (preferred level) — no redline proposed.**

Section 18 (¶¶ p0073–p0074) satisfies every preferred INSURANCE element:

| Element | Document |
|---|---|
| CGL USD 1M per occurrence | "at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence" |
| CGL USD 2M aggregate | "USD 2,000,000 aggregate" |
| E&O USD 2M | "professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000" |
| Cyber USD 5M where Customer Data processed | "cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000" (unconditional, so broader than our conditional ask) |
| Workers' comp as required by law | "workers' compensation as required by law" |
| Certificates on request | § 18.2 "On request, Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance" |

Vendor also carries a one-year post-term tail, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, primary-coverage wording, notice of cancellation/material reduction, and confirmation that insurance does not limit its liabilities — all Customer-favourable and left untouched. Additional-insured status is not in the checklist; noted only, not flagged.

**Finding: WARRANTY — compliant (no redline proposed).**

Section 19 of the Silverline agreement clears the fallback checklist in full and most of the preferred position:

- **Professional/workmanlike + documentation conformity** — 19.1 covers both for Services and Deliverables.
- **Software duration** — "Services" (§1.7) is defined to include the hosted software, and 19.2 warrants hosted Services conform "throughout the subscription term," well beyond the 90-day floor; Deliverables get 90 days from the later of delivery or acceptance.
- **Remedies** — 19.4 provides re-performance/repair/replacement at no charge plus a refund of Fees paid, and is expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims.
- **Compliance with law and malicious code** — 19.3.
- **Disclaimer does not swallow the warranty** — 19.5 is mutual and expressly preserves express warranties, service levels, indemnities and stated remedies.

Noted in the rationale rather than redlined: the Deliverable conformity period is 90 days rather than the preferred 12 months (the hosted software runs term-long anyway), and the malicious-code warranty is limited to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor." These are sub-preferred details, not fallback failures, so we accept the clause as drafted.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.",
  "Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination."
]

- **Responsive clause:** Section 7.6 (p0032) — the only Customer-payable liquidated amount in the document. Searches for liquidated damages, penalties, early-termination/minimum fees, dependency mechanics, and termination payment obligations returned no other hits; § 7.3 (disputed amounts) and § 21.1 (mutual cap) do not create or cure a Customer LD.
- **Why it fails:** USD 25,000 per day accrues for *any* dependency delay, with no materiality threshold and no ceiling, so it breaches the fallback (early-termination fee capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount) and can exceed remaining contract value — walk-away territory.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.

Finding rationale:
Section 7.6 imposes USD 25,000 per day of agreed liquidated damages on Customer for any delay in providing a dependency. That is a Customer-payable liquidated damages charge, triggered by even a minor or immaterial dependency slip and uncapped in duration, so it fails the fallback (which permits only an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount) and sits in walk-away territory because the daily accrual can exceed remaining contract value. No other clause creates a Customer-payable liquidated amount or early-termination fee, and the mutual cap in Section 21.1 does not cure it. We therefore take the preferred position and replace the charge with an unconditional confirmation that Customer owes no liquidated damages or penalties; nothing else in Section 7 or elsewhere cross-references 7.6 or retains a related payment mechanic.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.",
  "Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination."
]

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.",
  "Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination."
]

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.1: "Vendor may audit Customer no more than once every 12 months" — replaces the original "at any time without notice."

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.1: "on 30 days' written notice".

elements.element: Audits occur during business hours.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.1: "during business hours".

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.1: "by an independent auditor".

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.1: independent auditor "bound by confidentiality obligations".

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.1: "off-site where possible".

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained 22.2: "Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall."

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: Retained 22.2: "Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly"; the conflicting remote-access permission in original 22.1 ("may remotely access Customer's systems and records") is deleted, so no contradictory retained sentence remains.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.1 caps audits at "no more than once every 12 months", which satisfies a once-per-year cap.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Rendered 22.1 requires "30 days' written notice", which exceeds the 15-day minimum.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained 22.2 shifts costs to Customer at an underpayment "exceeding five percent", not ten percent; read literally the fallback threshold is not present. This is the preferred-level formulation, so the preferred checklist is nonetheless complete and no repair is needed.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: Not a fallback element; noted only for completeness — 22.2 bars direct system access and the walk-away remote-access language is removed.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the single replacement of Section 22.1 supplies frequency (once per 12 months), 30 days' written notice, business hours, off-site where possible, and an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, while the already-protective cost-allocation (5%) and no-direct-system-access language in Section 22.2 is left intact.

The walk-away features of the original clause (unlimited, unannounced audits and remote access to Customer systems) are eliminated, and the deletion also cures the internal conflict with the no-direct-access sentence in 22.2.

Minimal: one surgical replacement of the offending sentence, no survival tails, procedures, expense allocations, remedies or other extras added, and no Customer-favourable retained language removed. Section 22.2 is untouched, so there is no duplicate cost or access mechanic.
Preserves intent: Vendor retains a usage-audit right and the shortfall/cost-reimbursement mechanic; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created.
The fallback cost element (10% threshold) is not literally present because the contract uses the preferred 5% trigger; this requires no repair since the preferred checklist is fully met.
Severity remains medium; the finding is correctly classified as a deviation because the original 22.1 failed even the fallback (no frequency cap, no notice) and reached walk-away territory.

content.text:
**Finding: TRANSITION — compliant (meets preferred).**

Section 11 of the agreement already delivers our full preferred checklist:

- **11.1** — transition assistance triggered "Upon expiry or termination for any reason," for "up to six months," priced at the expiring Order Form rates (at least as favourable to us as then-current rates), and expressly covering knowledge transfer, export support, replacement-supplier cooperation and continued service levels.
- **11.2** — return of *all* Customer Data within thirty days in a "complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format," with metadata, and no hold-back for fee disputes.
- **11.3** — secure deletion of remaining copies and written officer certification, sequenced *after* we confirm successful return, with any law-required retained copy remaining protected and use-restricted.

Corroborating provisions (10.1 post-termination rights through the transition period; 16.5 deferring Customer Data to Sections 11 and 15) are consistent and create no conflict.

Two non-material points noted for the record only, not redlined: the 30-day return clock runs from our request rather than from termination itself (we control the trigger, and no pre-expiry request deadline is imposed), and assistance pricing is anchored to the expiring Order Form. Neither is adverse to us, so no change is proposed.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-56e30d01","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.","rationale":"Section 20 meets the preferred position in full. 20.1 gives an express Vendor duty to defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates against third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims relating to the Services or Deliverables. 20.2 extends the Vendor indemnity to Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud. 20.4 supplies the standard procedure (prompt notice, reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, control of the defence, with a materiality-of-prejudice qualifier and a settlement-consent protection favouring the indemnified Party). Customer's reverse indemnity in 20.3 is properly narrow, covering only unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized and Customer's violation of Applicable Law, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination or instructions. 20.5 additionally provides the fallback-level procure/modify/replace remedies with a refund of prepaid and implementation Fees (straight-line three-year basis) and bars termination of unaffected Services. The fallback super-cap of 3x annual fees is unnecessary and would be adverse to us: under 21.3 indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims and therefore uncapped. The permissive fallback exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) are absent from 20.1, which is more favourable to us. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-f2df7ecb","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 13.2 For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.","rationale":"The IP package meets our preferred position in full. 14.1 confirms Customer ownership of Customer Data and independently developed IP and limits Vendor's rights to processing solely to provide, secure, support and improve the Services for Customer (service delivery, not independent exploitation); 15.1 reinforces this and any other use requires our express written consent, so there is no standing Vendor licence. 14.2 vests ownership of each Deliverable in Customer on creation with an express Vendor assignment of all worldwide right, title and interest plus personnel assignments. 14.3 preserves Vendor Technology only, and 13.2 grants us and our Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to embedded Vendor Technology with modification and contractor-support rights. 14.4 rules out joint ownership absent a signed instrument. The only sub-preferred detail is that Deliverable ownership in 14.2 is \"subject to payment of the applicable Fees\" — noted, not a deviation, and no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-67e7dfdd","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.","rationale":"Section 21 meets the preferred position on its material terms and therefore sits above the fallback. The cap is expressly mutual (\"each Party's total aggregate liability\", \"The cap is mutual\") and is set at the greater of Fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. \"Fees\" (§ 1.5) means recurring subscription, professional services, usage and other amounts payable under an Order Form, so the 12-month basis is substantive rather than illusory. Section 21.2 excludes indirect and consequential damages mutually and confirms restoration of Customer Data, replacement services, notices and incident response are direct damages. Section 21.3 places confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other Party's IP wholly outside the cap, and confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not damages. Section 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities, and no warranty, indemnity or service-credit clause imposes any lower or one-sided cap. The only point short of the preferred wording is that the payment carve-out is expressed as \"undisputed Fees for conforming Services\" rather than all amounts due; that is a minor sub-element noted here rather than a deviation, so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-506eac42","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.","rationale":"Section 24 meets our preferred position in full. 24.1 gives Customer a consent-free right to assign to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all assets (prompt notice only, which is not a consent condition). 24.2 bars Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent, with the reasonableness standard running in our favour, and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor. 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any termination, suspension, repricing, acceleration or service-reduction right on our change of control, so we are clear of walk-away territory. 24.3's residual mutual consent requirement applies only to \"other assignments\" and therefore does not cut back the 24.1 carve-out, and 13.3 aligns by letting Customer transfer licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with a Section 24-permitted assignment. Only minor point short of ideal wording: 24.2's competitor bar is expressed as \"without Customer's consent\" rather than absolute, but that leaves the discretion with us and is noted rather than redlined.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-ef5789c9","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.","rationale":"The first Section 2.2 imposes full-term exclusive dealing on Customer for hosted analytics services with no category limitation beyond that service line, no 12-month cap, and no automatic exit on service-level or delivery failures — walk-away territory under this rule and a failure of the fallback on every element. It also conflicts with Section 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and Section 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity commitment). We take the preferred position and convert the appointment to non-exclusive rather than negotiating a narrowed exclusivity, which also removes the internal inconsistency.","proposal":"Convert the first Section 2.2 from a sole-and-exclusive-provider commitment to a non-exclusive appointment with no Customer exclusivity obligation.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-e4497af0","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.","rationale":"Section 7.6 imposes USD 25,000 per day of agreed liquidated damages on Customer for any delay in providing a dependency. That is a Customer-payable liquidated damages charge, triggered by even a minor or immaterial dependency slip and uncapped in duration, so it fails the fallback (which permits only an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount) and sits in walk-away territory because the daily accrual can exceed remaining contract value. No other clause creates a Customer-payable liquidated amount or early-termination fee, and the mutual cap in Section 21.1 does not cure it. We therefore take the preferred position and replace the charge with an unconditional confirmation that Customer owes no liquidated damages or penalties; nothing else in Section 7 or elsewhere cross-references 7.6 or retains a related payment mechanic.","proposal":"Remove the USD 25,000 per day Customer-payable liquidated damages and confirm Customer owes no liquidated damages or penalties.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-459b1b85","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.","rationale":"The licence provisions meet the preferred position in full. Section 13.1 grants the subscription/access right to \"Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf\" for their internal business purposes, so affiliates and contractors are covered without any notice condition. Section 13.2 grants a \"perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence\" for paid-up software and Vendor Technology (including material embedded in Deliverables, confirmed by Section 14.3). Section 13.3 bars Vendor from revoking or suspending a licence \"except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure,\" so the subscription licence is not revocable at will. Section 13.3 also permits Customer to transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24, and Section 24.1 lets Customer assign without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets; Section 24.4 further blocks Vendor from repricing or terminating on a Customer change of control. Section 13.4's use restrictions are narrow (reverse engineering, interference, security bypass, unlawful use) and expressly do not limit authorized security testing or use of Customer Data and output, so they do not cut back the grant. No redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-d97cc5f2","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.","rationale":"Section 12.3 affirmatively preserves our freedom to develop, acquire, licence, sell or use any product or service and to conduct business in any field or territory, and records that we have given no non-compete commitment. That satisfies the preferred position (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer), so no redline is needed. No other clause imposes a competitive or field-of-use restraint on us: Section 2.1 confirms there is no purchase commitment, and the Section 13.4 use restrictions (reverse engineering, interference, security bypass, unlawful use) are ordinary acceptable-use terms, expressly not limiting authorized testing or use of Customer Data and output. Section 2.2 (Vendor as sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services) is a sourcing exclusivity commitment and belongs under the EXCLUSIVITY rule — it restricts who we buy from rather than what business we may operate or what we may build, so we do not double-flag it here; it should also be reconciled with the contrary acknowledgement in 12.3 when EXCLUSIVITY is addressed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-97a27484","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 8.1 This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms. Expiration of this Agreement does not itself terminate an Order Form then in effect; this Agreement continues to govern that Order Form until the Order Form expires or is terminated.","rationale":"Section 9 grants only for-cause rights: material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2) and Customer's Vendor-default triggers (9.3), with 9.5 addressing cross-Order Form effect; 27.3 is a force-majeure exit and 6.2/19.4/20.5 are remedy-specific. No convenience termination right exists anywhere for Customer despite a three-year term, which is walk-away territory under T4C, so the fallback is not met either. Vendor likewise has no convenience right today, but silence gives us nothing to quote, so the inserted clause states it expressly; Section 8.2's 180-day non-renewal mechanic is a renewal term and is not flagged here. Inserted Section 9.4 in the existing numbering gap carries the preferred elements: 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and no Vendor convenience right during a committed term.","proposal":"Insert Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience termination right with pro-rata refund and confirming Vendor has none during a committed term.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-32443d92","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.","rationale":"Section 22.1 permits unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems, which is walk-away territory and fails even the fallback (no frequency cap, no notice period). Sections 22.2 and 22.3 are already protective: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds five percent, and Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, so only the frequency, notice, business-hours, off-site and independent-confidential-auditor limbs are missing. We conform 22.1 to the preferred position in one surgical replacement and delete the remote-access permission, which also removes its conflict with 22.2.","proposal":"Conform Vendor's audit right to once-per-12-months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, off-site, independent confidential auditor; remove unannounced remote access.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-5db0c71b","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.","rationale":"Section 28.1 selects New York law (and disapplies the CISG), and Section 28.2 gives the state and federal courts in New York County exclusive jurisdiction with irrevocable submission to personal jurisdiction and a venue/forum-objection waiver. The only carve-out is the customary right to seek temporary injunctive relief elsewhere to protect confidential information or IP, which does not defeat the exclusive merits forum. There is no arbitration provision anywhere in the document, foreign-seated or otherwise. The pre-filing executive escalation in Section 28.3 is time-limited (fifteen business days) and expressly does not delay urgent relief or filings needed to preserve a limitations period, so it does not impair access to the New York courts. This meets the preferred position on both elements.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-2931a78e","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 7.2 Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.","rationale":"Section 7.2 imposes an MFN running against us: we must extend to Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms given to any other technology supplier. It is open-ended — no defined product, no duration limit, and no like-for-like comparison carve-outs — so it fails the fallback and sits in walk-away territory. It also directly conflicts with Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. The shortest cure at the preferred level is to negate the obligation in Section 7.2, leaving Section 12.3 consistent; any Vendor-granted MFN in our favour would remain acceptable.","proposal":"Negate the Customer-side MFN obligation in Section 7.2.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-9508e255","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 2.1 This Agreement establishes the legal terms under which Customer and its Affiliates may purchase Services from Vendor. No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.","rationale":"The Agreement sits at our preferred position. § 2.1 (p0012) expressly states that no minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies and that Customer pays only for Services ordered in an executed Order Form, with a decision not to order further being neither a breach nor a shortfall. This is reinforced by § 7.1 (p0026), which bars any unstated minimum-use charge, and § 12.3 (p0050), in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment. Searches for \"minimum\", \"shortfall\", \"take or pay\", \"volume\", and \"prepaid\" surfaced no take-or-pay or volume-cap mechanic; the only \"shortfall\" references (§§ 22.2–22.3) concern audited underpayment, not a purchase commitment. The exclusivity language in § 2.2 restricts sourcing rather than imposing a purchase or volume commitment, so it is addressed under the exclusivity rule and is not flagged twice here. **From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook.
